speaker: dvm
text: Hi, this is Doctor Lindqvist from the clinic. Bella is under anesthesia for her dental cleaning, and she's doing well. Is now a good time?

speaker: client
text: Yes, I've been waiting for your call. Is everything alright?

speaker: dvm
text: Her heart rate is ninety and her oxygen is ninety nine percent, so she's stable. We've finished the cleaning and the dental x-rays.

speaker: dvm
text: We found two teeth that need to come out. The upper right fourth premolar has a slab fracture with the pulp exposed, and the lower left first molar has lost a lot of bone around its roots.

speaker: client
text: Oh. She did break a tooth on an antler chew about a month ago. I wondered about that.

speaker: dvm
text: That fits. Have you noticed her chewing on one side, or dropping food?

speaker: client
text: Yes, now that you mention it, she chews on the left and she drops kibble sometimes. And her breath has been really bad.

speaker: dvm
text: Those teeth are almost certainly painful. I'd recommend extracting both today, while she's already asleep.

speaker: client
text: How much will that add to the bill?

speaker: dvm
text: The two surgical extractions, with nerve blocks and the extra anesthesia time, add about six hundred and forty dollars.

speaker: client
text: Okay. We set a budget of one thousand two hundred dollars total. Will we stay under that?

speaker: dvm
text: Yes, with the cleaning that comes to about one thousand and fifty.

speaker: client
text: Then please go ahead with both extractions.

speaker: dvm
text: Thank you. I'll note that you approved both extractions by phone. She'll go home with pain medication.

speaker: client
text: She can't have the chicken flavored ones. She had a bad reaction to chicken, she gets itchy and her ears flare up.

speaker: dvm
text: Good to know. I'll record a chicken allergy. We'll send gabapentin capsules and meloxicam liquid, which isn't chicken flavored.

speaker: client
text: And what about food? She's on a hydrolyzed diet for the allergy.

speaker: dvm
text: Keep her on that, but soak the kibble in water for ten days so it's soft. No chew toys or antlers for two weeks.

speaker: client
text: No antlers at all, honestly. I'm throwing them out.

speaker: dvm
text: That's probably wise. We'll recheck her mouth in ten to fourteen days to make sure the gums have healed.

speaker: client
text: Okay. What time can I pick her up?

speaker: dvm
text: Around four thirty. We'll call you when she's awake.

speaker: client
text: Thank you so much for calling.
